text.p: Rockwell International Corp said Wednesday its Rockwell/Lockheed Martin Corp team has secured a $179 million contract from the the U.S. Air Force Space and Missile Systems Center.
The contract covers the design, development, test, launch and on-orbit operations of a flight experiment satellite and extends through 1999.
The demonstration/validation phase contract also includes the development and test of ground demonstration sensors and processors.

Rockwell's Space Systems division is the prime contractor, responsible for systems engineering and flight experiment operations. The satellite sensors will be built by Rockwell's Autonetics & Missile Systems Division and the spacecraft bus and launch vehicle will be constructed by Lockheed Martin Missiles & Space. Lockheed Martin Federal Systems will develop the ground segment.
Work on the contract is scheduled to begin this month. The flight experiment satellite is scheduled to be delivered in less than 27 months.
